summary:
Performance review of m2/hit-feel at 8f5519f. All probes are in /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-perf/captures/review_perf/. I measured in-process CPU per tick with a meter that splits each frame into scene _physics_process, the deferred flush (skeleton and ragdoll modifiers, Sprite3D redraws), physics step plus idle callbacks, _process, and render/present. I also logged the Performance pipeline-compilation counters. I ran one Godot process at a time. Load averages were 2.4-8.6 during runs. pgrep showed only my run plus the idle Godot editor (PID 7177). Every A/B was repeated 3 or more times. GPU timestamps read 0 on Metal, so GPU costs are vsync-off, GPU-bound frame intervals.

Phase 3's own code is cheap and does not leak:
- **Six ragdolls (headless):** six full ragdolls cost 1.35-1.41 ms a tick (median of 3 rounds × 2 processes; max 2.2-3.1 ms), against 0.30-0.46 ms idle. Six partial ragdolls cost 1.12-1.22 ms. The contact push changes nothing: 1.35-1.41 ms with it, 1.35-1.41 ms with a central kick. All six lie asleep 104-105 ticks (1.73 s) after the hit and are up at 137 ticks.
- **KO cycle:** 21 cycles of six dummies (KO, limp, blink, vanish, revive, blink-in). Nodes stay at 3936, objects at 10082-10092 and resources at 212, with 0 orphans. Joints stay at 102 and PhysicalBone3D nodes at 108, with 0 active physics objects at rest. Static memory is flat (169.75-169.90 MB without the meter). Six vanishing at once cost 0.86 ms; six reviving at once cost 1.1 ms.
- **Contact flash and the bars, per call:** hurt_point() 4.9 µs, flash_at() 13 µs headless, follow_flash() 0.3 µs, screen_anchor_of() 19 µs a bar.
- **Respawn checks:** _has_room() 2-8 µs. _respawn_spot() 8 µs when the post is free, 134-169 µs when blocked.
- **Hold view:** the hold view's ticks cost 1.3 + 2.0 µs. Frames while holding have the same median as standing (198 µs), so the hold view and the bend are negligible as expected.
- **Flash warm-up:** it works in both views, which answers the critic's open question. The first flash_at() costs 0.15-0.88 ms with it (n=8) and 3.3-8.7 ms without it (n=8), and a surface pipeline compiles only without it. The box sitting outside the first-person view does not matter.
- **Flash overlay, many at once:** six rigs flashing add 246 draw calls and about +0.24 ms of GPU-bound frame time at 5 m (+0.3-0.6 ms with three dummies 0.9-1.4 m from the lens). Toggling next_pass every tick on six rigs compiles nothing.

Known item (c) no longer reproduces. In 6 fresh real-time vsync runs, the first finisher's frames peak at 19.7 ms or less, the same as later finishers. Its only first-use cost is one canvas pipeline compile for the impact frame (0.9-3.4 ms of render CPU).

The cold-start hitch has moved to two places:
- **The first hit of any run:** the first comic sprite builds its material on the hit frame. That frame takes 7-20 ms of main-thread CPU, and real-time frames run 24-38 ms (finding 1).
- **The first bruise at the game's 30 hp:** the damage look's shader variant is rebuilt whenever no body shows a look (finding 2).

Both are pre-phase-3 VFX code. Both fixes are load-time warm-ups or a constant material variant, and neither changes behaviour.

open_question_notes:
From the performance side, the open items cost little, with one exception: option (c) of hit-02.
- **grab-05 and hit-01 (first-person flash size, flurry strobe):** none of the options has a performance cost. The overlay is drawn over the whole rig whatever its radius, so (b), capping the on-screen share, or (c), softening repeat flashes, costs nothing. The flurry's 7 on/off switches cost about 0.1 ms each (flash_at() in a window), and switching six rigs every tick compiles nothing.
- **Side-view flash minimum size:** a larger flash radius costs nothing measurable. The draw count is the same, with fewer discarded pixels.
- **hit-02 (a hit on the player in first person):**
  - Option (a), flashing the player's first-person arms, reuses the already warmed overlay.
  - Option (c), a HUD edge vignette, would be a new canvas material. Like the impact frame (finding 1), it would compile a canvas pipeline the first time it shows, so it needs the same load-time warm-up.
- **grab-03 and hit-03 (combat log):** no performance angle.
- **Known item (c), the first finisher's dropped frame:** not reproduced on this build. In 6 fresh real-time vsync runs, the first finisher's frames peak at 19.7 ms or less, the same as later finishers (up to 22.3 ms). Movie Maker steps a fixed clock, so no capture can show a dropped frame. The run's hitch is now on the first hit, and at 30 hp also on the first bruise (findings 1 and 2).
also_noticed: A sleeping full ragdoll still runs its modifier every tick (visual-pose FK, 22 bone followers moved, direct body states fetched): six asleep cost 0.50-0.64 ms/tick against 0.31-0.35 standing (about 30-50 µs a body). A knocked-down body sleeps only its last ~0.55 s (asleep at tick 104, up at 137); a KO body sleeps through most of its 2.5 s.

Each rig builds its ragdoll on its first ragdoll (Ragdoll.setup()): that receive_hit() costs 0.44-0.51 ms (0.97-1.33 ms for the run's first) against about 0.1 ms later. Milestone 3's crowds could prebuild at spawn.
A dummy with no free respawn spot re-runs _respawn_spot() every tick, at 134-169 µs per waiting dummy (17 room checks plus casts). That is fine now; a retry interval would help crowds.

A vanished actor keeps its full tick (animation, FK, hurtbox transforms): six gone dummies cost 0.49 ms/tick against 0.36 ms standing. Milestone 3's spawner should free them on vanished, as ARCHITECTURE plans.

Each finisher's two impact frames add about 5.3 ms (1.9-7.5, n=18) of GPU-bound frame time over the next three frames (the screen copy with its mip chain at 1600x900) on a ~9 ms GPU frame. This is within budget on the M1 and the largest GPU item measured.
flash_at() costs 0.09-0.9 ms in a window (13 µs headless) because of the RenderingServer material and next_pass updates. Fine, but the spin kick flashes three rigs in one tick.

Bot and probe exits print 'ERROR: N resources still in use at exit': 12 AudioStreamWAV clips (grunt/thud/whoosh) are still held by the audio voices at quit (--verbose list in hold_verbose.log). This happens at exit only and is not a runtime leak.
RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu() reads 0 on Metal on this machine, so GPU costs in this review are vsync-off, GPU-bound frame intervals.

The first heavy hit (first blood droplets, THROWN sprite) costs 4.0-6.4 ms CPU against 2.0-2.7 ms later. The first blood splat landing (LYING, shaded sprite, about 16 ticks later) adds about 1 ms to the deferred flush. Both belong to finding 1's warm-up set.

findings.title: The first hit of every fresh run drops a frame: the first comic sprite builds its material on the hit frame (only the contact flash is warmed up; the first finisher no longer drops one)
findings.detail:
In a fresh process, the first hit that spawns a comic effect (the first jab's light burst) spends 7-16 ms of main-thread time on the hit frame. The time goes into the deferred-call flush after _physics_process, which is where SpriteBase3D's deferred redraw runs and where the first ComicSprite (POP, no_depth_test) creates its 2D material and shader. One surface pipeline compile follows on the next frame (PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SURFACE 1). Later first jabs spend 0.3-0.5 ms there.

How it shows in play (real time, vsync on, 1600x900, Metal on the M1):
- Without a warm-up, the first hit's frame takes 35.8 / 32.4 / 29.1 ms at 500 hp and 37.8 / 23.8 / 24.3 ms at the game's 30 hp, followed by a 4-8 ms catch-up frame. In the first-hit window, 22% of frames run over 25 ms.
- With load-time warm-ups, the same frames take 18.2-23.4 ms, and no frame in that window runs over 25 ms (pre-play baseline: 0% over 25 ms).

Main-thread CPU on the first hit's frame (fixed 60 fps, vsync off):
- No warm-up: 11.5 / 15.7 / 20.2 ms (first person) and 18.0 / 10.6 ms (side view), of which the deferred flush is 5.8-16.4 ms.
- After spawning one burst and one word at load (the probe's --warm=big): 4.0 / 4.2 ms, and 3.1 / 3.2 ms in side view.
- With all warm-ups: 3.3 / 3.2 ms. The warm-up frame itself takes the hit at load instead (4-7 ms of deferred flush).

The same first-use pattern, smaller:
- **First heavy hit:** its blood droplets (THROWN sprite variant) cost 4.0-6.4 ms CPU against 2.0-2.7 ms later.
- **First blood splat:** landing (LYING, shaded) adds about 1 ms.
- **First finisher:** the impact frame (a canvas material with hint_screen_texture and mipmaps, hidden until then) compiles one canvas pipeline. Its first impact frame costs 0.9-3.4 ms of render CPU against 0.3 ms. Calling impact_frame.flash(0) at load removed both (pc_canvas 0, 0.3 ms). In 6 fresh vsync runs, the first finisher's frames peaked at 19.7 ms, the same as later finishers (up to 22.3 ms), so known item (c) no longer reproduces as a dropped frame. Its remaining first-use cost is this one compile.

HumanoidRig._warm_flash() is the only load-time warm-up, and it works: first flash 0.15-0.88 ms with it against 3.3-8.7 ms without, in both views.

findings.suggested_fix:
Warm the VFX director's first-use materials at load, the way _warm_flash does the overlay, only when a window exists:
- Once VfxDirector is in a windowed tree, draw one ComicSprite of each material combination it uses (POP with no_depth_test, THROWN, LYING shaded) once inside the camera frustum, tiny and for one frame, then retire them to the pool.
- Draw the ImpactFrame material once, for example on a 1 px rect for one frame, or during the first loading frame.

The probe's equivalent took the first hit to 3.1-4.2 ms of CPU, left no frame over 25 ms, and removed the finisher's canvas compile. Add a test that the warm-up exists in a window and is skipped headless.

findings.title: Every clean-to-bruised switch rebuilds the damage-look shader variant whenever no body shows a look: 3-5 ms on the main thread, 12-16 ms the first time in a run, a missed vblank on the first bruise
findings.detail:
set_damage_look(BRUISED) turns on detail_enabled and uv1_triplanar on the rig's paint materials, which is a different BaseMaterial3D shader variant. Godot keeps a variant's shader only while some material uses it. Once every body is clean again (in the test room, after every revive), the next bruise creates the variant again in the idle callbacks after the physics step, and a surface pipeline compiles on the next frame (PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SURFACE 1).

Measured on the switch tick (windowed, 2 runs x 3 rounds):
- **Bruise with no other body bruised:** 3.2-4.8 ms of main thread, the same for 1, 3 or 6 rigs at once (it is per event, not per rig). The first time in a process it took 11.9 ms.
- **First bruise in a fresh 30 hp P P P P:** 11.6-11.9 ms in 2 of 9 processes, 3.5-4.0 ms in the rest. At 500 hp, with no look change, the same tick takes 0.1-0.2 ms.
- **Another body kept bruised:** further bruises cost 0.2-0.3 ms (n=12), which confirms the mechanism. Holding the variant in a material that sits on no mesh does not work, because the shader is created lazily.
- **Detail layer always on, textures swapped:** 0.1-0.4 ms (n=18), no pipeline compile, and no measurable GPU cost at 5 m (median frames 9.01 / 7.30 ms against 9.28 / 7.25 ms).
- **Bruised to bloodied** is already only a texture change (0.1-0.4 ms).

In play (real time, vsync on, 30 hp, the second jab bruises):
- The first bruise's frame takes 32.9 / 26.3 / 23.3 ms, followed by a 4-9 ms catch-up frame.
- Later bruises, after a revive, give 20.8-25.0 ms late frames.
- With the load-time warm-ups, the first bruise's frame takes 20.0-23.2 ms.

This predates phase 3. Phase 1's review called it unmeasurable from vsync-bound frame intervals, which hide main-thread cost.

Sheet: sheet_damage_look.png. Code: game/fx/damage_look.gd:45-57 (apply() toggles detail_enabled and uv1_triplanar); game/actors/humanoid_rig.gd:524-527 (set_damage_look); humanoid_rig.gd:699-709 (_build_materials already keeps emission enabled so set_flash() never switches variants).
findings.repro: `godot --path . --fixed-fps 60 --disable-vsync res://captures/review_perf/probe_look.tscn -- --tag=t`, then read the LOOK rows of captures/review_perf/look_t.csv (step_us). Add `--hold` to keep one body bruised (the cost disappears). In the game, at the default dummy_health of 30: jab twice on a fresh dummy, and the second jab bruises it and hitches. After the dummy is KO'd and revives clean, the next bruise costs 3-5 ms again.
findings.suggested_fix:
Never switch the material variant. In _build_materials(), keep detail_enabled, MIX blending, detail UV1 and uv1_triplanar on for the bruisable paints, with a fully transparent detail texture standing for CLEAN, and have DamageLook.apply() swap only detail_albedo, the same trick set_flash() uses for emission. This looks identical and measured 0.1-0.4 ms per switch with no GPU cost seen.

The alternative is to keep one hidden mesh with a bruised material alive for the run, which holds the variant and compiles its pipelines at load.

Add a test that a damage-look change leaves the material's shader RID unchanged.
